name: GPA Converter
tagline: Convert percentages to letter grades and work out your 4.0 GPA.
title: GPA Calculator and Percentage Converter (4.0 Scale)
h1: GPA calculator and percentage converter (4.0 scale)
description: Free GPA calculator for the US 4.0 scale. Enter each course grade and its credit hours to get your GPA, or convert a percentage to a letter.
card_summary: Enter course grades and credit hours to get your 4.0 GPA, or convert a percentage to its letter grade.
lead: Pick the letter grade for each course and add its credit hours, and the calculator works out your GPA on the standard 4.0 scale. A percentage converter sits alongside it for turning a mark into a letter grade.
takeaways: On the plus and minus 4.0 scale, an A is 4.0, a B is 3.0 and a C is 2.0.
Your GPA is your total quality points divided by your total credit hours.
Percentage cutoffs for letter grades differ between schools, so check yours.
Schools that use whole letters only will get a different result.

sections.h2: How does the 4.0 GPA scale work?
sections.html:
US colleges turn each letter grade into points, then average those points across your credit hours. Uni2study sets out the 4.0 scale with the plus and minus values most US colleges use, and the table below follows it.

LetterGPA points
A4.0
A-3.7
B+3.3
B3.0
B-2.7
C+2.3
C2.0
C-1.7
D+1.3
D1.0
D-0.7
F0.0

sections.h2: How is GPA calculated with credit hours?
sections.html: Multiply each course's grade points by its credit hours, add those totals together, then divide by the total credit hours. A 4-credit B (3.0 points) contributes 12 quality points, which counts for more than a 1-credit A. Your cumulative GPA covers every term, not just the latest one.

sections.h2: How do percentages convert to letter grades?
sections.html: Schools set their own cutoffs. A common plus and minus version gives an A for 93 and above, an A- for 90 to 92, a B+ for 87 to 89, and continues down to a D- for 60 to 62, with anything below 60 an F. This US grading guide lists the full chart. The percentage converter on this page uses that common version, so check your school's own table if it differs.

sections.h2: What if my school does not use plus and minus grades?
sections.html: Some schools use only whole letters, so a B+ counts as a 3.0 rather than a 3.3. The calculator uses the plus and minus values, so a school with whole letters will get a different result. Use your registrar's scale in that case.

faq.a: A good GPA depends on the school, the course and what you want to do next. Ask your school or the programme you are applying to for their own benchmark.

faq.q: Is an A+ worth more than an A?
faq.a: At most schools, no. Many give both an A+ and an A 4.0 points. A few give an A+ more, so check your school's rules.

faq.q: Can I use this for a weighted GPA?
faq.a: Not directly. This calculator uses the standard 4.0 scale. Weighted scales give honors or AP courses extra points, so they need a different calculation.
